utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Niemann?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour. Your Honour, at some time convenient to the Chamber today, I would like to raise a matter with the Chamber in closed session in relation to Witness L in which an order applies relating to that. It is a matter for the convenience to the Chamber at some appropriate stage, but preferably as soon as possible.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Bos raised that with us and we can meet in closed session after our morning recess, if that is soon enough, is it?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: That is convenient, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Kay, would you call your next witness, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I call Jozo Popovic, your Honour. JOZO POPOVIC, called.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Sir, would you please take the oath that is being handed to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I solemnly declare that I will tell the truth, the whole truth and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: You may be seated. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Kay, you may begin.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Is your name Jozo Popovic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: What is your job, Mr. Popovic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am a teacher, a teacher.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Are you currently a teacher?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: When did you stop teaching?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Whereabouts do you live?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I currently live in Kozarac.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: For how long have you lived in Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Since 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Where did you live before then?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I lived in the village of Bosanska Bojna in the municipality of Velika Kladusa.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: When did you leave Velika Kladusa to come to the Kozarac region, if you can remember the date?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Finally, September 15th 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I would like you now to look at a map so that we can have these places in mind. Prosecution Exhibit 78, please. If you could just take a few moments, Mr. Popovic, by looking at that map, perhaps locating where Prijedor, Banja Luka and Velika Kladusa are? Then if it could be put on the monitor beside you so that we can point these things out and see them on the screen? There should be a pointer, a steel pointer, on the desk in front of you, Mr. Popovic. If that could be extended and perhaps the map laid flat? If you turn to your right and point on there, first of all, where Banja Luka is. Perhaps if we could come in closer on the map? That is fine. If you could point, first of all, where Banja Luka is?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Here. [The witness indicated].

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: And where Prijedor is?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [The witness indicated] Here.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: And where Velika Kladusa is?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [The witness indicated] Here.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Could the map be moved down the screen a little bit more? Much more than that, so that Velika Kladusa is -- that is fine. Can we go a little bit further into the map? Can we go a little bit further into the map, please? Stop there. Just keep the pointer on Velika Kladusa. Can you tell us where Bosanska Bojna is which is the village you come from?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is a bit north of Velika Kladusa, here.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Is it between Glina and Velika Kladusa?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, exactly halfway between.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: If we can move the map down the screen a little bit more? We can see Glina there. If you just put your pointer on Glina? Thank you. For how many years had you lived in Velika Kladusa?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I lived in Velika Kladusa since 1964.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Were you born in that region?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Which region do you originate from?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was born in the village of Otok, the municipality of Ogulin, the Republic of Croatia.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: What is your date of birth?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: August 10th, 1941.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Are you a married man?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Can you tell us what your family consists of?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The members of my family are my wife, Petra, son Sasa, and son Sinisa.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Was your wife a teacher as well?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: When did she stop teaching?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: She virtually has not stopped except for a brief period during -- between June, that is June or July of '92 until August, that is September 1992, when she started working as an educator in Hrnici.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: When we heard your evidence a moment ago, you said that you stopped teaching in 1969, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: What did you do from 1969 onwards?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: For three and a half years I worked temporarily in the Federal Republic of Germany. After 1974 I moved back to Velika Kladusa where I worked in Kladusnica which is a company that provides services.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: What work were you doing there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At the beginning I worked as a receptionist in the Hotel Konak for four months. Then I was a chief receptionist for two months. After that I started working in the personnel department and I was the head of the personnel until 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Your son Sasa, how old is he? What is his date of birth?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sasa was born on December 5th 1972.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Your son Sinisa, what is his date of birth?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was born in August 1974.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: What was the reason for you leaving Bosanska Bojna?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I left because of the war, because of the war activities.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: At that time did you leave on your own or with other people?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: With other people.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You said that the starting date for your living in Kozarac was September 15th 1992. Had you actually visited Kozarac before that date?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: When was that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was there twice, several hours each time; the first time in July 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: When was the second time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not recall exactly the date.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: When you came to settle on September 15th 1992, was that when your wife moved to also live in Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did your son Sasa move at that time to live with you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: What about your son Sinisa?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Has he ever lived with you in Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Has he visited you in Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Once.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Where did your son Sinisa go when you left Bosanska Bojna?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He went to Topusko.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Where is Topusko?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Topusko is to the south of Glina, about 30 kilometres from Bosanska Bojna.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Is that due south of Glina?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I could not tell you exactly -- I assume, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: If we were to put that map in front of you again, although Topusko is not marked, would you be able to show us the general place where it would be found?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I could.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Perhaps if Exhibit 78 could be put back on the monitor again? If we can focus in on that left-hand corner of Bosnia where Velika Kladusa is found?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Right here.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: If the map could be brought down the monitor quite a bit? If the map could be brought right down on the monitor so that Velika Kladusa is in the middle? Thank you. Could you point out where Topusko is to be found on the map? Keep your pointer on it for about five seconds.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [The witness indicated].

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you very much. So that is to the west of Bosanska Bojna, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is possible. I said it was south of Glina by my assessment.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you recollect when your son Sinisa has visited you at Kozarac, when that was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot recall exactly the date, but I know it was a weekend. It was a Saturday and a Sunday.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Whereabouts is your son Sinisa at the present?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: What was the reason for him not coming to Kozarac with you when you moved there in 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was a student in the high school specialising in mathematics in Velika Kladusa and since the war operations started right after the end of that school year, after he finished a third year in the school in Velika Kladusa, he moved to Topusko to the same school because there were no war operations going on there. So then he finished the fourth year. After that he entered into the university and school of forestry in Banja Luka, and he lived there. Before the last exodus, before September 1, 1995, he went to do his regular national duty, military duty, in Petrinja, and with the fall of Krajina he withdrew with the relatives, the kin that we had there, to Belgrade and he continues to live there to date.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: In 1992 when he was at the school in Topusko, who was he staying with?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He lived with his uncle, my wife's brother, and his family.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did your son Sinisa ever work as a guard at Trnopolje camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I would like to ask you now some other questions about after you moved to Kozarac. Which particular part of Kozarac do you live in today?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In an area that is called Suhi Brod.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Is that south of what is called the new Prijedor/Banja Luka highway?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: The house that you live in today, was that the first house you moved in to when you arrived in the area from Velika Kladusa?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Was that house empty when you moved into it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Do you know who owned it previously?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Who was that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Ibrahim Nukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: At that time did you have anywhere else to live yourself?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: What had happened to your former home in Bosanska Bojna?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The house remained. However, after -- because of the war operation the windows and doors were broken and the floor had been ripped up and for a while there was only the roof. After that I do not know what happened to the house.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: When did you last see it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In May 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You described the final exodus from Velika Kladusa as being September 1st 1995, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not understand the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Were there a series of movements of people from the Velika Kladusa area from 1992 onwards?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, people were moving for two months.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: When you arrived in Kozarac did you meet a man called Dusko Tadic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Had you known him before you arrived in the area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Can you tell us what dealings you had with Dusko Tadic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The first contact we had when he arrived with some other people to my home, and Bozo Dragicevic was there with him, Goran Babic, Milenko Zigic and another man, and I do not know his name. They came to talk to me about the organisation of life of the new people who arrived in this area.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Why did they come to see you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They came to me because I came with these other people from Bosanska Bojna and those people needed to be included into the life to organise the survival there. Since I was the President of the Local Commune there, the people who they got in touch with referred them to me so they came to me to discuss what we should do next.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did you get involved with the Local Commune in Kozarac at this time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: What work were you involved with in relation to the Commune?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: First of all, I joined in the activities of the political party there, the Serbian Democratic Party. I was also a member of the Executive Committee of the Local Commune in Kozarac and I was a member of some temporary provisional commissions at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: What temporary commissions were you involved with at that time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: First of all, I was a member of the commission for agriculture, because we needed to organise the fall sowing, and it was a task of the commission to organise that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Other than the agricultural commission?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There were other commissions for reconstruction of the economy. We needed to reopen the mill where we would deal with the crops. Then the commission for water works, and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: At this time in autumn of 1992 were there many refugees that had come to the Kozarac area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: From the territory of Velika Kladusa there were 150 households who moved to this area, and we also found other people from other regions of Bosnia and Herzegovina, from Jajce, Livno, Travnik -- maybe some others, I do not know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Are you able to put a figure for us on the number of people at this time that had moved into the Kozarac area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was roughly about 500 people, to the Local Commune of Kozarac and the Local Commune of Trnopolje, there were also people who had come to settle. I do not know the exact figure because I did not keep any records there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Was Trnopolje run as a separate commune from Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We came as part of the organisation of Trnopolje, but the settlement in this Local Commune, the commune of Kozarac, the two separated. The affairs of one Local Commune from the others were separated.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. Kay, would you ask the witness whether there were 500 people or 500 households.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Your Honour, yes. [To the witness]: The number you gave us of people coming to the area in autumn of 1992, you gave the figure of 500. Was that 500 people or 500 households?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: 500 people and I said about 150 households.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Was that from Velika Kladusa at this time or from the other areas that you told also had refugees moving into Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Only from Velika Kladusa.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: The figure I was actually seeing if you could help us with was the total number of people, not only Velika Kladusa but those from the other regions as well in the autumn of 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, there were more than that, but I do not know the exact number.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Subsequently in 1993 were these numbers added to by more people coming into the region?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You told us that you joined the Executive Board of the Local Commune. Did you also join the SDS Party in Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Had you previously been a member of the SDS?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: When had you joined that Party?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I joined in 1990 when it was founded in Velika Kladusa.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: The area that you came from in Velika Kladusa, were you a minority ethnic group in that area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. We constituted less than one per cent of the total population.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: What is your ethnic group?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: When you joined the SDS Party in Kozarac, did Dusko Tadic have a position in the Party at that time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, he was President of the local committee of the Serbian Democratic Party in Kozarac.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: In the autumn of 1992 can you tell us how many members of the SDS there were in Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: According to the records he had, there were over 100 members. I took over these records from him, and I looked through them and brought them up-to-date. The number was reduced because some people had moved.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did you actually yourself have a position in the Party at a later stage?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was the Vice President of the Party, of the local committee of the Party.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: When did you get that position of Vice President?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Somewhere around October 1992, if I remember well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did you ever obtain a position higher than Vice President?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I was President of the municipal board of the Serbian Democratic Party of Velika Kladusa before moving.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did you remain as Vice President of the Party in Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did Dusko Tadic remain as President of the local party?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He did.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did there come a time when he left Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know what you have in mind. For a short period or for a longer period?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: For a long period, left Kozarac permanently?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Somewhere in August 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did someone else become President after him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, after some time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Who was that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you. I would like to look at some documents now. The first one is Prosecution Exhibit 155. If that could be put on the monitor? Put it on the monitor in English and put the Serbo-Croat in front of the witness and that will be easier. Thank you. This is a document, Mr. Popovic, that has been introduced in evidence in this case. Can you see your name on it as No. 2?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do. I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Can you tell us what the referendum on 15th and 16th May concerned?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: At this stage were you an ordinary member or were you Vice President or some other position?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I was Vice President.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you. Perhaps if you could look at another document which is No. 156? If the English could be put on the monitor and the Serbo-Croat in front of the witness? This is dated 20th May 1993. We can see it is recorded there that you are Vice President, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: We can see from the information on this piece of paper that it is an extract from "Election report on staffing of the local committee of the Kozarac SDS. After a visit and check on the work of the Kozarac local committee members, the local committee was reelected and members from Jaruge, Kozarusa, Podgradje, Hrnici and Kozarac town centre were elected". Then it is signed on the right-hand side. Can you tell us, first of all, as to the scale of the Party, the SDS in Kozarac, at this time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I said that there were around 80 members.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: From your evidence we can determine that far more people lived in the area than were members of the Party?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You worked with Dusko Tadic who was President of the SDS in Kozarac at this time. What was the main object of the Party's work in Kozarac from the fall of 1992 until August 1993?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, the Serbian Democratic Party is a political party which means that it engaged in political activity. Within that scope, it proposed certain personnel solutions for the Local Commune. It assessed the political situation, and through its representatives in the executive bodies of the Local Commune it would implement that policy.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: The Local Commune that you have referred to, did Dusko Tadic also have a position in that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: What was his position?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was Secretary of the Local Commune.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did you undertake any work for the Local Commune as well? You have told us about the commissions you were involved in, but did you work on behalf of the Local Commune in any other way?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I said already that I was a member of the Executive Board, which at the time had 12 members.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: What were the concerns of the Local Commune at this time from the autumn of 1992 till August 1993?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Would you please repeat the question?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: With what was the Local Commune involved in that period from autumn of 1992 until August 1993?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I already said that in view of the fact that we had only just come to these parts it was necessary to first accommodate people. That was our task No. 1. Then we had to revive the work of the elementary school so the children should continue their regular education up to 4th grade of elementary school. Then we needed to organise the health service to provide space, facilities, a doctor; then enable the functioning of the veterinary service, for the local people to have regular supplies of electricity, water; then we had to distribute relief, humanitarian aid, to refugees and people in need; to maintain contact with higher level bodies in the municipality, both at the Party level and at the administrative level in the municipality; also to keep in touch with humanitarian organisations in Prijedor and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did you ever take over Dusko Tadic's role in the Local Commune after he left Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I took over the position of Secretary in October 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: During this period from autumn of 1992 and August 1993, but particularly during 1992, did you see Dusko Tadic regularly?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: About how frequently?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Almost every day, except for the weekend, and some days when Dusko attended meetings in Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Could you see how he spent his time then at this stage from autumn of 1992 until the end of the year of 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In Kozarac.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: What was he doing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Most frequently he was in the premises of the former elementary school where both the Party and the Local Commune were based, that is, where he held meetings, received people or he was on location within the territory of the Local Commune touring the remaining economic facilities, visiting and so on, working on the ground, so to speak.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Was he Commander of the collection centre at Trnopolje at this time in 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Were you aware of the fact that there was a collection centre at Trnopolje during this period?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You have described Dusko Tadic's work in the commune of Kozarac and in relation to the SDS. Did he work hard at these two jobs? Did they occupy his time, so far as you could see?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it was hard work. It required work, so to speak, around the clock, from morning till night, and it was the time of war.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Your Honour, at this stage because of other matters that I want to deal with in relation to this witness's evidence, we should go into closed session.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: We will stand in recess for five minutes to go into closed session. Then we will discuss the matter that you wanted to discuss as well, Mr. Niemann.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: (The Court adjourned for a short time).

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Your Honour, whilst the witness is being fetched, may I deal with a couple of housekeeping matters which concern amendments to the transcript that the Registry have been good enough to provide? There were some translations during the video link that the parties agree were mistranscribed. If I could just indicate them to the Court? The first concerns page 5400 of the transcript during the evidence of Mr. Samardija, line 13. His evidence was recorded as being, "I think when the war began here in these parts in '42", the correction I have been given is of "'92". The next page concerns page 5406, line 26, which read, "They knew me and Tadic but, believe me, I did not know them and I do not know them until the present day" should read "They knew me and my sister". I believe those have been served on the Prosecution as well and all parties are agreed in those matters.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: That is correct, Mr. Keegan?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: That is correct, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Very good. Thank you, Mr. Kay. Mr. Keegan, you may begin cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour. JOZO POPOVIC, continued.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Mr. Popovic, I take it "Jozo" is your given name and not a nickname, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, it is not "Jozo", it is "Jozo".

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Did you have a nickname?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Your wife's maiden name, the last name, the family name, is that "Grmusa"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: If could I have the usher -- if you would show this document first to the Defence and then to the witness? Mr. Popovic, I am going to show you a piece of paper with a name on it. What I would like you to do is indicate to me whether or not that name is a relative of your wife -- the name of a relative of your wife, but do not say the name out loud, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Could you please just tell us what the nature of the relation is -- brother, cousin, uncle?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: My wife's brother.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, if we could have that marked as the next Prosecution Exhibit, please? That would be ----

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: That will be 358.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: 358 will be admitted and sealed. The transcript says, nature of the relation, brother, cousin, uncle and you say "wife's brother". OK. Thank you, sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Mr. Popovic, you indicated that you were the President of the Local Commune in Bosanska Bojna prior to the war?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: And that you had joined the SDS upon its founding?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Do you remember approximately when it is you became a member of the Party?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Somewhere in August 1990.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: You have continued to be a member since that date, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: During that time you have advocated and supported the policies and positions of the SDS, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: You indicated that your final move to the Kozarac area was in September, September 15th, I believe, 1992, but that you had visited the area on two occasions before that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Can you remember the date of your very first visit?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot remember the date, but it was in July 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Did you move your group of 150 families to the Kozarac area as a result of a meeting that you had in June 1992 in Bosanska Bojna with leaders from the SDS of Prijedor as well as Simo Drljaca?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: There was no meeting in June 1992 in Bosanska Bojna with members of ----

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There was a meeting,. There was a meeting, but not only with representatives of SDS, but with Presidents of the municipality of Prijedor, Bosanski Novi, Bosanska Krupa.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Who was the President of the Prijedor municipality who attended that meeting in June '92?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was Dr. Milomir Stakic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: He was also a member of the SDS, correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Did a man named Simo Drljaca also attend that meeting in June '92?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He did.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: What was the purpose of this meeting?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was an information meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: This meeting took place at the beginning of June '92?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: After this meeting did you continue to have contacts with the SDS officials from Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, neither before nor after, not until we moved to Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Your visit in July, what was the purpose of your visit in July '92 to that area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: To see the areas to which we planned to move.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: When was it that you started planning to move to that area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That was left up to every family to decide individually.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Again what was the impetus, what was the reason, why you chose to move to the Kozarac area as opposed to any other area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Because there were seven of us members of the commission assigned to see what the conditions of life were in this part, in this region, and to convey our impressions to the people living in Bosanska Bojna. We said what the area was like geographically, what the quality of the soil was, what the infrastructure was and other conditions, and families decided themselves whether they wanted to come there or to two other municipalities that were offered to them for resettlement or even to stay where they were living. It depended on their own decision.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: The other two municipalities were the other two that you mentioned that came to that June meeting?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Bosanski Novi and Bosanska Krupa. Those were their names at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: This whole issue of resettlement was organised by the SDS?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not the SDS, but by the bodies of the Municipal Assembly of Prijedor and at the time the command of the locality of Bosanska Bojna. It had no direct connection with the SDS.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: You indicated that you sent your son Sinisa to Topusko to continue to go to school?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: The reason that you sent him there in part was because there were no war operations going on there, correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In Topusko there were none, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: You indicated you had family there as well?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: You testified later on in your direct when discussing the conditions in Kozarac and the responsibilities for the Secretary of the Commune that, in part, it was difficult because the area was in war conditions at that time. My question is why would you choose to move to Kozarac which was in the midst of war conditions if, in fact, you could have gone to Topusko where there was none and you also had family? What was offered to you in order to convince you to move to the Kozarac area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the first place, I did not go to Topusko because this brother-in-law of mine, my wife's brother, was living in an apartment with one room with his wife, his daughter, then his wife's brother's son was also there going to school and my son. So really there was no room there. In view of the fact that most people opted for resettling in Kozarac, I decided to move there with my family primarily because we would be provided accommodation and there were other farm buildings that were available to move the cattle that we had, the livestock, and we were told that we would temporarily be able to till the deserted field, that we could invest in them.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Your son Sasa who moved with you to the Kozarac area, was he employed in Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Did he ever work at the Trnopolje camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He did.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: When was that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know exactly, because he was a conscript and it was the army that made the assignments.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: On how many occasions did you visit Trnopolje camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The camp itself, not once, but near the camp, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: When you say "near the camp", what do you mean by that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I said before that we came within the framework of the organisation of the Local Community of Trnopolje, and I had to contact with the staff that was based in, headquartered in, Trnopolje, and that distributed the houses we were moving into. So that I would just pass by the camp because from Suho Polje to the staff headquarters I had to pass by the camp and that was the only contact I had with the camp.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: As to your son Sasa, can you tell us what year or month he began working at the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was not work. It was his military duty. I do not know the date, but he knows exactly, because he did not just go there to guard the camp; he was a member of a Unit, of a military Unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: What Unit was he a member of, if you recall?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At first, the 43rd motorized, and later it became the 5th Kozara Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Where was the military Unit's base or headquarters in the area of the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: You did not go visit your son when he was on duty there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Which son?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Which of your sons were assigned there in addition to Sasa?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not one of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: So, obviously then it must be Sasa. Did you not go visit him when he was assigned to duty there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: You have indicated that you were a resident of, assigned to, the Mjesna Zajednica of Trnopolje, the Local Commune of Trnopolje. How was it that you were then invited to become an official of the Kozarac Local Commune?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We came within the organisation of the Local Commune of Trnopolje, but we were not members. We were not residents of that Local Commune, but we in a sense seceded from it when we arrived, and a member of the Executive Board -- I became a member of the Executive Board by election. An Assembly Meeting of citizens elects members of the Executive Board. I was proposed and I was elected.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: If Prosecution Exhibit 156 could be shown to the witness again, please? (Handed). If you could put the English copy on the Elmo, please, so that the Court can see it? Mr. Popovic, this is the document which you were shown earlier. If you could move it so that that top paragraph is on the screen? If it could be focused down a little so the whole paragraph can be seen? Thank you. Mr. Popovic, I would like to direct your attention to the paragraph that is above the list of names. The language indicates that after a visit and check on the work of the Kozarac local committee members, the local committee was reelected, etc. My question is, who was it that came to visit you and check on your work?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not understand the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: OK. Does that paragraph which is just above the list of names begin with the phrase "After a visit and check on the work of the Kozarac local committee members"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I have a different text before me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: OK. What does your text say?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: "In accordance with the initiative on visiting and checking the work of the members of the SDS local committee, the reelection and filling in of vacancies of members of the local committee was carried out with members from Jaruge, Kozarusa, Podgradje Hrnici and Kozarac".

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: OK. So my question is, who was visiting and checking on the work of the members of the SDS local committee?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The work of members of the local committee is controlled or, rather, it reports to the Assembly of the Serbian Democratic Party and the Assembly consists of all members of the local committee and they do the checking and the reelection.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: So the members of the local committee visit and check their own work and then reelect themselves? Am I understanding you correctly?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You did not understand me correctly. The Assembly of the Serbian Democratic Party consists of all members of that Party, and they propose and elect from within their ranks the members of local committees. So it is not the local committee that reelects itself; it is elected by the Assembly which consists of all members of the Party.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Approximately, how many members of the SDS were there in the Kozarac area at this time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At that time when these other hamlets were covered by the Local Commune, these that are listed here, Jaruga, Kozarusa, Podgradje, it had more members. Later, these localities, Jaruga and Kozarusa, were separated and they formed their own Local Commune, and so that members of the Serbian Democratic Party then their number was reduced. But at the time of these reelections, as far as I can remember, there were over 100 members of the SDS Party and that number was later reduced with the separation of these localities.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: At the bottom of the page on the right is a signature block. Whose signature is there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: You do not recognise that signature?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can see that it says "Tadic" and, as he was President at the time, I assume that it is his signature, but I cannot claim with certainty.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You are welcome.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: If I could just go back for a moment to the issue of Trnopolje? You indicated that with respect to being a part of that Local Commune you had contact with the staff that was based in the headquarters in Trnopolje, and that in going to that location you would pass by the camp. Can you tell me where that staff headquarters was located?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was located on the road from Trnopolje to Prijedor, about one kilometre away in a house, a private house.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Was that house on the left or the right-hand side of the road as you were going towards Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On the left, on the left-hand side, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: What was the colour of that house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think that the facade was white. I know there was a kind of a verandah in front.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Where were the offices of the local staff, what part of the house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On the ground floor, to the right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: How many floors were there in that house, do you recall?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think there was a ground floor, and maybe just a loft but I cannot remember exactly. There was an auxiliary building attached where meetings were sometimes held.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: With respect to the duties of the Secretary of the Local Commune, you discussed the responsibilities and the nature of those duties to some degree. Is it also true that the Secretary of the Local Commune worked in close co-operation with the local authorities in Prijedor itself?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: With the bodies of the Municipal Assembly, yes, because he is actually an employee of the Assembly.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: With the President of the opstina Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When necessary.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: When you took over those duties, did you, in fact, have meetings with Milomir Stakic about Kozarac and Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, only as a deputy at meetings of the Municipal Assembly. When Dr. Milomir Stakic chaired the Assembly meeting, I attended it as a deputy, but personally I did not have any contacts with him.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: You talked about seeing the accused Dusko Tadic frequently in the fall of '92, that most frequently it was in the local school, but that he would have to travel throughout the area visiting economic facilities, visiting refugees, etc., frequently, day and night, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not say at night, but he did during the day.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Did you have a vehicle of your own, a personal vehicle?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Was that a white Golf?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Did you ever loan that vehicle to Dusko Tadic so that he could conduct his responsibilities as a Secretary of the Commune?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, never.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Did you travel around in your white Golf when you were conducting your duties?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Keegan, would you ask the witness if the Golf belonged to him personally or the municipality?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour. [To the witness]: I asked you earlier if you had a personal vehicle and asked if that was a white Golf. Did you, in fact, own that car yourself?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: You indicated that the inhabitants of Kozarac still receive humanitarian aid, is that so?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Who directs that aid to those people?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: A Commission for Humanitarian Aid which has four members, of which one represents the Local Commune, one represents the refugees and misplaced persons, one is a member of a family of killed veterans and disabled from first to fifth category.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Who are those people, can you give us their names, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Just now this duty is being performed by Mr. Marcetic Zoran, as Chairman of the Commission, Zoran Marcetic, Zeljko Grmusa, member, Dragomir Crnogorac, member, and Branko Mitrovic, member.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: In the homes which the people from Bosanska Bojna and yourself live in in the Trnopolje area, if, in fact, the original owners of those homes returned to the Trnopolje area, is it your understanding that you would have to move out of those homes and find a new place to live?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Of course we will.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Just a moment, please, your Honour. Nothing further, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Kay?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You were questioned about the meeting in June 1992 of the municipalities of Prijedor, Bosanski Novi and Bosanska Krupa. Was Dusko Tadic present at that meeting?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you. That is all I ask. Mr. Keegan, do you have additional questions?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: No, your Honour, I do not.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Is there any objection to this witness being permanently excused?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour, there is.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Pursuant to our earlier discussion, then Mr. Popovic you are free to leave. However, you may be recalled as a witness perhaps this week. So you should keep in touch with Mr. Kay and make yourself available but you are free to leave now. Thank you for coming.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: All right, thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Miss de Bertodano, would you call your next witness?

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour. The next witness is Sinisa Popovic. SINISA POPOVIC, called.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Sir, would you please take the oath that has been handed to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I solemnly declare that I will tell the truth, the whole truth and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Fine. Thank you. You may be seated.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: Witness, is your name Sinisa Popovic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: Where do you live?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: How long have you lived there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: One year.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: What is your ethnic group?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Serb.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: What is your date of birth?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: August 18th 1974.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: If this document could be marked as Exhibit 81 and given to the witness?

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Does the Prosecutor have a copy of that Exhibit?

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: Your Honour, yes, and I have copies for the Bench and copies also of a translation. Perhaps if the Exhibit could be marked as A and the translation as B?

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, could we possibly be told what marking is on that Exhibit?

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: 81 -- it is No. 1A and B. 1A will be 81A and 1B, 81B.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Usher, would you show it to the Prosecution? Then please show it to the Prosecution and then we will have it marked.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: Your Honour, they have a copy, I believe, that they have identified it.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: OK. Do you have a copy now?

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour, we have what was marked as 1A and 1B.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: That is what is 1A and 1B?

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: Your Honour, yes.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: OK, good.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: Mr. Popovic, is that your birth certificate?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: Does it have on it your father's name?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: What is your father's name?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Jozo.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: You have told us that you live in Belgrade. What is your occupation in Belgrade?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I work with a private entrepreneur.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: What sorts of job do you do?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Those are carpentry, woodwork, works.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: Have you studied carpentry and woodwork?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: Before you lived in Belgrade, where did you live?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Topusko.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: When did you complete your education?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I completed in June 1993, that was the high school. Then I started -- enrolled in Banja Luka at the university in the fall of 1993, and I still have the status of a student to date.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: Did you study in Banja Luka?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: What did you study?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: A school of forestry.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: If I could have this Exhibit, which is for the Prosecution No. 2A and B, marked as 81A and B.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Is there any objection to 81A and B, that was the previous one, the birth certificate?

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: No, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: 81A and B will be admitted. This will be 82A and B.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: One again, there are copies for the Bench. Witness, do you recognise this document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: What is this document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is a certificate that I was enrolled in the first semester of the school year, the academic year 1993/94 as a full-time student.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: You told us that before you went to study in Banja Luka you were studying in Topusko, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: When did you graduate from the school in Topusko?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In June 1993, I think. I do not know the exact date.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: If I could have this document marked as 83A and B and that is 3A and B for the Prosecution. If 83A could be put in front of the witness. Mr. Popovic, do you recognise that document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: Can you tell us what it is?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is the certificate of the completed fourth grade of the elementary school in Topusko, the natural science and mathematics department.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: Does it give a list of your grades and then an overall mark?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: What was the overall mark?

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: Could I have this document marked as 84A and B, and that is 4A and B for the Prosecution. If 84A could be put in front of the witness. Do you recognise that document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: What is it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is a certificate about the exams that were the balance. That is the exams, the additional exams I had to pass in order to get my certificate, my diploma.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: What is the date on that certificate?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: March 11th 1993.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: When did you take those exams?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Several days before the certificate was issued.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: For how long were you at the school in Topusko?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: One school year, 1992 to '93.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: Where had you been at school previous to that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Before that I went first, the first year of the secondary school in Bihac and then the second and third in Velika Kladusa.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: If these documents could be marked 85A and B, and that is 5A and B on the Prosecution list. Mr. Popovic, do you recognise that document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: What is it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is a certificate about the completed third year of the secondary school in Kladusa.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: What year is it dated?

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: You finished school in Kladusa in 1992, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: Where were you living at that time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In Bosanska Bojna.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: Did you continue to live in Bosanska Bojna during the summer of 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Up until August, end of August 1992.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: What happened at the end of August 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Because of the war operations I had to take refuge from there.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: Where did you take refuge?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I went to Topusko.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: Where did you go to live in Topusko?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In March Eighth Street with my uncle.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: Is your uncle your mother's brother or your father's brother?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He is my mother's brother.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: Where did the rest of your family live at this time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In Prijedor, more precisely in Kozarac.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: When did they move to Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think it was at the end of August or beginning of September.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: What does the rest of your family consist of?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I have a brother Sasa and a father and a mother.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: Did they all go to live in Kozarac at this time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: Did they all go there together?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think they did.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: When you were in Topusko living with your uncle, did you go and visit your family in Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: When did you first go to visit them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The first time I visited them in February '93.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: Had you visited them at all in the area of Prijedor before that date?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Before that I visited them in August '92, but I was not in the home. But we saw each other in Prijedor, in the city.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: How long had they been in the area of Prijedor at that time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Maybe several days.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: Had they yet settled in the home that they found near Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think that they did, but I am not 100 per cent sure.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: Which members of your family did you see in Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: My brother.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: How did you travel from Topusko to Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: A tractor.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: Was anyone travelling with you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: My brother and two friends or three.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: Is that your brother Sasa?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: How long did you stay in Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Several hours.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: Did you see your father in Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I did not see him.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: Did you return on the same day to Topusko?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: How did you travel back?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Again with my brother Sasa.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: Did your brother Sasa then stay in Topusko with you or did he return to the Prijedor area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He then went to Bojna, you could still go there at that time, and then after that he went back to Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: Do you know when it was that he went back to Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know exactly.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: When you visited Prijedor did you visit any other villages in the area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: When did you start your school year from 1992 to '93?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: September 2nd.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: At what school was that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That was the secondary school Bogdan Orescanin.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: Who was the head teacher at that school?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Vojo Pavlovic.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: Did you have a class teacher in addition to the head teacher?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, there was Milica Paic.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: Did Milica Paic teach you any individual lessons in addition to being your class teacher?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, she did physical education.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: Was a register taken of your attendance at the school in Topusko?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: How often was it taken?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Every day at class.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: Were you ever absent during the year of 1992 after September 2nd from the school in Topusko?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: What days of the week were you in the school?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Monday through Friday.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: At weekends did you stay in Topusko or did you travel elsewhere?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mostly I was in Topusko.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: Did you ever travel out of the area of Topusko during 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know. Maybe I would go to another part of Krajina or Glina Petrinja.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: Did you ever travel to Prijedor after the visit you told us about in August 1992 and before the end of 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: Did you see your family at all during that time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they were coming to visit me.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: Did you know where they had settled?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: And where had they settled?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In Kozarac, near Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: Was that in the town of Kozarac itself or in a neighbouring village?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think it is a village. I think that Kozarac itself is a village.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: Did your family live in Kozarac or in a village outside Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot tell you exactly the demarcation between Trnopolje and Kozarac. I think the hamlet was called Hrnici.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: Did you visit your family in Hrnici at any time during 1993?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: When was it that you first visited them in 1993?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think it was February 16, '93.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: For Prosecution purposes this is No. 8 of the bundle. There are three copies for your Honours. If that could be marked as Exhibit 86. Your Honours, there is presently no translation of that. What I intend to do is to get the witness to read out the document so that it can be translated onto the record. Then we will get a translation of the document at a later date.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Do you wish to offer Defence Exhibits 82A and B, 83A and B, 84A and B and 85A and B?

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: Your Honour, yes.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Any objection?

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: No, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: They will be admitted. Is there any objection to 86? The witness is going to read it.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: I do not know yet, your Honour. I do not know what this is.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Of course. We will have read it. It will go into the record and then we will rule on any objection. OK.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: Mr. Popovic, do you recognise that document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: What is it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: A certificate.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: Because we do not have a translation of it I would like you to read the document from the top to the bottom so that it can be translated in court for the record. So if you could start from the word "Srednja skola" at the top and read right through to the bottom.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: "At the secondary school Bogdan Orescanin in Topusko the certificate. Hereby, it is certified that Sinisa Popovic, son of Jozo, born August 18, 1974 in Bihac, municipality of Bihac, state of Bosnia and Herzegovina, the full-time student of the school Bogdan Orescanin in Topusko in the school year 1992/93, that he is enrolled in the fourth year. This certificate is issued in order to allow free movement from Topusko to Prijedor and cannot be used for any other purposes." Then a date 1993 and a secretary of the school, Milica Paic.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: What was that date in 1993?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: February 16, 1993.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: If you turn that document over there are some markings on the back of it. Can you tell us what those markings are?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Those are some numbers which I took down while I was playing cards.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: Your Honour, I offer that document as No. 86.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Is there any objection?

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: No, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Defence 86 will be admitted. We will stand in recess until 2.30. 1.05 p.m.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Wladimiroff and Mr. Keegan, are you delighted to be back in this courtroom?

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, as a matter of fact, I felt like Mr. Bean being in Banja Luka.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: It was an interesting perspective on that side of it, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: We feel like we are enclosed sometimes and in a fish bowl, but we learn to appreciate it, I guess, when we encounter other circumstances. SINISA POPOVIC, continued.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: You may begin, Miss de Bertodano.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour. Examined by MISS DE BERTODANO, continued.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would ask that Defence Exhibit 86 be placed in front of the witness again? Mr. Popovic, before the luncheon adjournment you read out that document to us. I would like you to tell us now what was the purpose of that document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At that time I could not leave Krajina when I wanted to go and visit my parents because of certain circumstances, and with this pass I had no problems. It was easier to pass.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: Did you have to show this pass anywhere?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, at the crossing between the Republic of Serbian Krajina and the Republika Srspka at Dvor Na Uni.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: During that school year, was this the only pass that you got of this nature?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: Was this the only time that you visited the area of Trnopolje during this year?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: On what other occasions did you visit the area of Trnopolje?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: After February. I think it was in June, end of June, in '93.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: Was that after you had completed your school year?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, just before.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: When you went to see your family on this occasion on 16th February 1993, how long did you spend with them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: A few days.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: Where did you go to after you had seen them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Back to Topusko.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: Were you aware that at any time there was a collection centre in Trnopolje near to where your family lived?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: How were you made aware of that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not know directly, but from hearsay.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: When did you hear about it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, shall we say, in January '93.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: Who did you hear about it from?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: From friends of, I do not know exactly who, the rumour was, whether it was true, I did not know.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: Did you ever visit that collection centre?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: Did you ever work as a guard at that collection centre?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: Your Honour, at this point I would ask that we go into closed session.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Let us see. Cross-examination is not going to be conducted on that matter that we go into closed session for? I was thinking that, perhaps, we might go into cross-examination and then go into closed session and hear both sides.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: I have no objection to that, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: I do not think that will work. Then we will stand in recess for five minutes to go into closed session.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Miss Hollis?

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour. SINISA POPOVIC, continued Cross-examined by MISS HOLLIS, continued.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, one other matter concerning Prosecution Exhibit 359, we would ask that that be under seal.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Yes. It will be under seal 359.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour. [To the witness]: Mr. Popovic, you indicated that you moved to Belgrade about a year ago, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
