utterances.text: Where did you live before you lived in Belgrade?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Topusko.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: During the time you went to school in Banja Luka where did you live?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Also in Topusko.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: So you commuted back and forth each day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I had a flat in Banja Luka.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: So, how many days of the week would you remain in Banja Luka?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Depending, sometimes five, sometimes over the weekend, so that would mean 14.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: I am sorry. You said sometimes five days a week and sometimes you would also remain there over the weekend, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: What was the period of time that you went to school in Banja Luka, from what month and year until what month and year?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: '93, early September, is when I left for Banja Luka to start, and then the academic year ended June '94. So then there was a summer vacation until September of '94, that means -- which means that is where the academic year resumes.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: You spoke about a trip that you took to Prijedor in August 1992, a trip that you took on a tractor. Do you recall when it was in August 1992 that you made that trip?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am not sure. I think it was somewhere around 20th August. I am not sure.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: Why did you go to Prijedor on that occasion?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I wanted to buy some clothing, some personal clothing, for myself.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: Who went with you on that occasion?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: My brother Sasa and some friends. I think there were two or three that went along.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: At this time was your brother Sasa living with you in Topusko?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: Where did you go to meet with your brother Sasa before you continued on to Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: To Glina.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: Then from Glina you went to Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: Did you actually go to the town of Prijedor or to some area around the town of Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I stayed in the town looking for what I wanted to buy while the brother went to Kozarac, to that house where my family moved to.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: Do you know how your brother went from Prijedor to your family's house in Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: With that tractor which we took to come to Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: Do you recall the names of any of your friends who went with you on this trip to Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think it was Slobodan and Stanko.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: Slobodan's last name is what?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not remember.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: Stanko's last name, do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: How long did this trip take you to go from Glina to Prijedor by tractor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: About four maybe even five hours.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: The return trip from Prijedor back home, how long did that take you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: About the same.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: You were shown an Exhibit, Defence Exhibit 86, which you indicated was a certificate which allowed you to travel in February 1993. Do you recall that certificate?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: Is it correct that when you made your travel to see your family there was only one instance when you had to show that certificate?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: That was when you crossed from the Republic of the Serbian Krajina into Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, no other questions at this time. We would reserve further cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Miss de Bertodano?

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: Nothing arising, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Sir, you are excused at this time and you are free to leave. However, you are subject to being recalled so you should make yourself available. Please keep in touch with Miss de Bertodano. She will notify you whether it is necessary to return, probably this week -- is that correct -- or early part of next week?

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: That is correct, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Thank you. You are now free to leave. Thank you very much for coming.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Kay or Miss de Bertodano, call your next witness, please.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour. The next witness is Milica Paic. MILICA PAIC, called.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Would you please take the oath that is being handed to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I solemnly declare to speak the truth, the whole truth and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Fine. Thank you. You may be seated.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Miss de Bertodano?

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: Witness, is your name Milica Paic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: What is your ethnic group?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Serbian.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: Where do you live?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I now live in Serbia, Pozarevac.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: What is your occupation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: A professor of physical education.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: Are you teaching at present?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I started two weeks ago.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: How long have you lived in Pozarevac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Fourteen days.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: Where were you living before that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: From '95, August of '95, until fourteen days ago, I lived in Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: Did you teach when you lived in Belgrade?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: Where did you live before you lived in Belgrade?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Before Belgrade I lived in Krajina, in Topusko.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: Were you teaching when you were living in Topusko?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: How long had you lived in Topusko?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: 26 years.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: How long had you been teaching there for?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: 25 years.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: What school did you teach in in Topusko?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In a secondary school, high school, technical school.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: Did that school have a name?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, the secondary school Bogdan Orescanin, Topusko.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: Were you teaching in that school in the school year of 1992 to 1993?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, up until 1995.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: What was your position within the school?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was again a professor. My class was physical education. That is what I did.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: Did you have any other duties in relation to the students beyond teaching physical education?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I was always a class teacher and then I had other duties relating to athletic activities in certain clubs and such.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: Was a young man called Sinisa Popovic ever in your class?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, he was. He was a student in my class.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: Can you remember what year that was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He came to Topusko in '92, in the fall, so that was the school year of '92/93, and he was enrolled in the final fourth year of the school.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: Was that the only year that he spent in your school?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: When you were teaching during 1992 and 1993 did you take a regular record of your students' attendance?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that was one of my duties as a class teacher and of the other colleagues who taught there. They were there to -- they had to record the attendance of the students but it was my particular duty to so.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: How often would you do that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Twice a week, and then at the end of the week we had summaries of the entire attendance of all students throughout the week.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: Would you notice if a student was absent for any period of time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Of course, my colleagues, other teachers, would also note that during their classes.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: When you were teaching Sinisa Popovic, do you recall whether he was a student who was absent for periods of time or whether he was a student who attended classes regularly?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sinisa Popovic was a full-time student. That was his status, but not only his status, but also he was present there at all times. He was one of the -- one with the -- one of the best attendances.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: How often would you see him during the school week?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Every day because he lived in the same block, apartment block, where I lived and then I would also see him in the school daily.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: Would you see him outside school hours?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. He was also active in sports. The club that I led, he was playing soccer and then, as I said, he lived in the same apartment block. It was a different entrance. He was living with his relatives so I could see him on a daily basis.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: Did you see him at weekends?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sometimes, because we lived close to one another, but I mostly spent my weekends either on the sport fields or fishing, not every weekend, I cannot claim that I have seen him every weekend, but I have.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: Could Defence Exhibit D84A be put in front of the witness? (Handed). Mrs. Paic, do you recognise that document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: What is it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is a certificate that Sinisa had to pass the balance of exams because the programme of the school in Kladusa where he was enrolled beforehand was different from the one that he attended in Topusko. So he had to pass a balance of exams, and this is the certificate about him having passed those exams.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: When would he have taken those exams?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He had a deadline to take those exams. I think it was about four or five months within which they had to do it, but I think it was February or March and that is what it says here too.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: Who is that document signed by?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This document was signed by the school master at the time, Vojo Pavlovic, the principal.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: Thank you. If that document could be given back to the Registry and if D83A could be put in front of the witness? (Handed). Mrs. Paic, do you recognise that document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, this is a certificate about completed fourth, final year and I actually wrote this one up and I signed it as class teacher.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: Is that your signature on the bottom left-hand side of the document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes, this is my signature.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: When was that document created?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This document was created at the end of June of 1993.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: That was the end of the fourth, final year of school for Sinisa Popovic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, after that he had his final exam.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: Were there any school holidays, regular school holidays, between the start of the school year in 1992 and the end of December 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, there were some regular school holidays. There was a holiday for St. Nicholas which is 19th December and some others I cannot recall.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: Were these long holidays or holidays for a single day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is one working day.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: Were there any holidays during that period for more than one working day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As far as I recall, no, but maybe they were linked to a weekend, that one day would be linked to a weekend.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: If a student of yours wished to have time away from school, whose permission would he have needed to get?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: According to the rules and law of the secondary education, it was me as a class teacher, any leave for up to three days. Up to five days, it would be incumbent on the principal, and then over that it would be the teachers' council. So that was in the law.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: Do you recall Sinisa Popovic asking for such time off during 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I recall that he once asked for an absence, leave of absence, to go and visit his parents, but I cannot say whether it was '92 or '93.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: Could document D86 be put in front of the witness, please? (Handed). Mrs. Paic, do you recognise that document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. I also signed this document.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: What is the document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is a certificate that Sinisa was given permission to travel from Topusko to Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: Does this relate to the occasion which you recall that he asked for leave of absence to go and see his parents?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am not sure if that is because to any student I could give him permission to leave for a day or two, so he would not need this certificate. He needed this, a certificate, so I did not need it, but he needed it so that he could move from Srpska Krajina to Republika Srpska, but when I was giving them permission I did not need any certificates.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: As far as you recall, is this the only certificate that you gave him of this nature?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: Thank you. I have nothing further.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Cross-examination, Miss Hollis?

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Ma'am, during the school year 1992 and 1993, were there Christmas holidays that would have lasted more than a day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, because Christmas was celebrated on January 7th, and that was anyway winter holiday time from December 31st until February 1st, the students had a holiday.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: So between the time 31 December and 1 February, the students were not in class, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that was the regular holiday.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Were there any other times during the school year where they had a similar break?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, there were not any holidays but there were breaks in the teaching process. As a result of assessments of the security situation or perhaps due to lack of heating in the winter months, then school would be interrupted for two or three days but these were not holidays, except for the holiday I mentioned, St. Nicholas, and maybe some others I cannot remember.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: So then, if I understand correctly, there was this break between 31st December and 1st February, and there may have been other breaks depending upon the security situation, the weather, such things?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: You mentioned attendance records. Where were those attendance records kept?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The records of all full time students were kept in a registry which I am sure still exists in Topusko and they can always be looked at. They are kept in safe keeping.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, no further questions at this time. We would ask to reserve cross-examination, if necessary.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Additional questions?

utterances.speaker: MISS DE BERTODANO
utterances.text: No, thank you, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mrs. Paic, you are excused now. However, you are subject to being recalled as a witness before the Tribunal. Therefore, you should make yourself available if you are asked to return to give testimony. So keep in touch with Miss de Bertodano and she will tell you whether it is necessary for you to return, but you are now excused. Thank you for coming.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Kay, would you call your next witness, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: The usher has just gone out of Court, but it is Dragoje Jankovic who will be in open session.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: I thought maybe he knew the order. He does not know about the next witness -- he should. He is doing a pretty good job. We will wait a moment. DRAGOJE JANKOVIC, called.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Sir, would you please take the oath that is being handed to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Thank you. You may be seated.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Kay, you may begin.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Is your name Dragoje Jankovic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Do you live in Gornji Orlovci near Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: What is your occupation, Mr. Jankovic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: My occupation is a technician and I am now working in a firm ----

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Is that firm in Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: --- for administrative affairs, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: How old are you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am 35.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Is your ethnic background that of Serbian?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Are you related to Dusko Tadic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: What is that relationship?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am his sister's son.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I will ask that question again. What is your relationship to Dusko Tadic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Cousin, a cousin.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you. How long have you known him for?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In time, you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We have known each other for a long time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you. Were you close to him in the family?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, we were not close, but like normal relatives.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Have you ever been mobilized for the JNA or the army of Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: By the army of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: When was that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At the beginning of 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Have you done your military service in the JNA?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: When was that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot remember the year. Just a moment, please. It was in 1980, '81.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Where were you when Kozarac was attacked in May 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was mobilized defending Serb villages, surrounding Kozarac.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Whereabouts were you stationed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In Gornji Garevci.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Are you familiar with maps of the area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Perhaps if you would like to look at Exhibit 79? I will change that -- sorry to do this -- to Exhibit 280 which is clearer. Can you see this map which contains Kozarac and Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Are you able to see whereabouts you live on the map in Gornji Orlovci?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Would you be able to indicate that to us if the map is placed on the overhead projector to your right? You will see the steel rod, if you could point on the map whereabouts it is. Hold your pointer on there for a few seconds. Can we have the camera back, please? Are you pointing there to the place where your house would be found?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: If again the camera can come back to show more of the map? Can you indicate with that pointer whereabouts you were at Gornji Garevci whilst the attack on Kozarac was taking place?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [The witness indicated].

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you. If I can ask the question this way: when were you first stationed at Gornji Garevci?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot remember the date exactly, but it was during the time of the beginning of the conflict around Kozarac.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: For how long did you remain stationed at Gornji Garevci?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Until we were carrying out the assignment entrusted to us, until the Unit was not -- was transferred elsewhere.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: How long then did this take?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Until August.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: From August where did you then go?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Our Unit was transferred to the region of Gradacac.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: When were you discharged from your mobilization with the army?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: After the signing of the Dayton Treaty. I do not remember the exact date, but that was at the end of '95 and the beginning of '96.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Whilst you were on duty in Gornji Garevci during the conflict in Kozarac, did you come across or see Dusko Tadic at all?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I saw Dusko Tadic for the first time when I was on leave, then he came to my house.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Can you recollect when that was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not remember the exact date, but it was in May.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Can you recollect what the purpose was of him coming to your house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Dusko came to see us to leave some of his things which he had saved from his house in Kozarac.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: At that time where were you stationed precisely?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The same place that I indicated to you, Gornji Garevci.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Were you at home for a period of time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That was a short leave and that is when I saw him.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: At this time when you saw him and you were at home for a short leave, for how long had you been at Gornji Garevci doing your duty there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot say exactly, but I said that it was in May. I do not remember how long for.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Can you remember when the conflict in Kozarac was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not the date.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Was it before the conflict in Kozarac or after the conflict in Kozarac that you saw Dusko Tadic on this occasion?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This was while the conflict was still ongoing.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: What do you mean by that? Can you explain that to us?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This was a time when we were protecting the Serb people and protecting civilians, Muslims who were there, to save people from the conflict and to ensure for them free passage and simply to save the lives of civilians.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Was there shelling of Kozarac at this time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, a little, for a short time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Can you recollect when there was a great deal of shelling and Kozarac was shelled for some three days?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: For three days -- I do not remember that it lasted for three days. It was brief at the beginning of the conflict itself and it lasted a short while.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you. I would like you now to look at three photographs.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: May I ask the witness, was the visit by Mr. Tadic then after this shelling, this short period of shelling, or before the shelling, in May?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This was, as I said, while the conflict was still going on and when the Serb people and army was doing its job, that is, to save civilians and their property, because Dusko managed to salvage some of the things from his home just then.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: So it was while the shelling was going on, is that what you recall?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, no, no, not while the shelling was going on.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: I will leave it to you lawyers to see if you can come up with a better date and, if not, I will try again at the end.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I will try again, your Honour, thank you. (To the witness): The shelling was not going on at that time then?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, it was not going -- when he came to see me there was no shelling.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: What did he bring when he came to see you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He brought some of his things from the house.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Can you tell us what they are?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: A refrigerator, some dishes and other things, basic householdware.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did he come on his own or was he with anyone?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At the time he was with another man.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Do you know who that other man was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Brane Koncar.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Do you know how they travelled to your place with these goods?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They came in a small vehicle, type Tam, TAM.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Do you know whose vehicle it was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I do not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Do you know who was driving the vehicle?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know the driver.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Were the goods on the vehicle that were left at your place just the property of Dusko Tadic or did the other man leave any goods at your place?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Just Dusko Tadic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: How long were they at your place for?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They stayed there for sometime, so that later Dusko would come and take what he needed when he found temporary accommodation in Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Were these goods ever collected?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Were you there when they were collected?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was not there then, because he would take them at -- some things at a time when he got his flat in Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Were you where when he collected any of these things?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was on duty.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Where on duty?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On duty, as I said, defending villages by the army, as part of the army.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: But where were you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The place, you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Gornji Garevci.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: How long did these goods remain at your place for?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You mean, in time?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot remember the date, but anyway the things were taken away and I cannot remember exactly because I was not at home when they were taken away.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: So when the goods were left at your place by Dusko Tadic, the shelling was not happening in Kozarac at that time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, not at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Can you recollect how long after the shelling of Kozarac it was that he came to your place to store these goods?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: A few days afterwards when things settled down a bit.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you. I would like you now to look at some photographs -- these have been supplied to the Prosecution in advance, your Honour -- and tell me if you recognise the general location where the photographs are taken. I tender them to the Court as D87A, B and C. Do you recognise the place that these photographs show?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is Gornji Orlovci and it is the place where Dusko worked at the police checkpoint.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Your Honour, there are three copies here for the Bench. I offer the Court these photographs as Exhibits.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Is there any objection to 87A, B and C?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: No, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: They will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you. Your Honour, it is really for illustrative purposes. As we have heard so much about checkpoint Orlovci, it is a way of showing the Court finally photographs of what we have heard so much about.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: At what point in time were these taken?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Very recently, within the last ----

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: I am sure you will ask the witness -- I mean, you will ask him what it looked like then?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Your Honour, yes. [To the witness]: These photographs show the place where that checkpoint was at Orlovci today, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Are you able to describe how the checkpoint looked in the times of 1992 during this period of the conflict?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You want it short or long?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Heads or tails!

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: There is a man standing here. Maybe when we come back from the recess he can, kind of, tell us where at least on these photos were the items that we have heard about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Your Honour, yes.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: OK. So we will stand in recess for 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STEPHEN
utterances.text: Mr. Kay, do you happen to know what "Gornji" means?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: No, your Honour -- "upper" I am told by those more learned in these matters.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STEPHEN
utterances.text: Then "Dornji" means lower?

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Kay, you may continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour. Mr. Jankovic, looking at those photographs now that are in front of you, do you see the first one which has a man standing in the middle of the photograph ----

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: --- beside a large tree?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: In relation to that photograph, can you tell us where the checkpoint was placed in 1992 after the conflict in Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The checkpoint was placed immediately to the left of this man.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: So that is slightly further up the road?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, it is to the left of the man, towards Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you. How was the checkpoint structured? What did it consist of?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It consisted of several, two actually, containers that were protected by sand bags.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Were those containers on both sides of the road?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, only on this side where this man is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: In relation to the large tree we see behind the man, were the containers off the road or on the green verge or on the brown bit which looks like a lay-by?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were next to the road in this -- on this brown part which means outside of the main roadway, off the main roadway, where the vehicles are moving.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: In the second photograph, photograph D87B, again we see the tree, we see a puddle and we see a tractor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Were the two containers side by side running along the road?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, alongside.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Were they in that general area between the tractor we see and the tree or were they somewhere else, if you could tell us from photograph B?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, in the vicinity of the tractor, next to the tractor.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Was there any kind of obstruction in the road to cause vehicles to slow down?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At that time there were obstacles, the so-called serpentines.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Were they some kind of obstacles that traffic had to slow down to get through and pass the checkpoint?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: When you say "serpentine", do you mean that the traffic had to go through a bending section of obstacles rather than just driving straight along the tarmac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You had to avoid them and before that you had signs for speed reduction.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you. The third photograph, D87C, is a photograph of the lane that we just see a part of opposite the "no overtaking" sign in photograph A.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Do you know Slavica Lukic at all?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Slavica Lukic, no -- maybe Radoslavka Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes, Radoslavka Lukic being her full name, do you know her?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Can you tell us if she lives up that lane we see in photograph C?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is a local village road leading towards her house.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: How far up that lane in photograph C would you say that she lived?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know exactly, but, say, up to 250 metres to the right of this road.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: We can see some buildings in the background of the photograph. Do you know if any of those are her house -- if not, say so?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, right. Her house is towards the end of this development. That means it is in the middle of it but to the right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: We see some roofs there in the background. Do you know if any of those roofs would belong to her house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is not visible from here, but I think the last photograph ---

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: --- on the right-hand side.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Is that on the right-hand side of the lane we see?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Is her house close to the lane? Does her garden come up to the lane?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Her house is immediately adjacent to the road.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you used to travel through checkpoint Orlovci during this period after the conflict in Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: How often would that be?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I passed when I was free, when I had leave to go from my Unit. That means that would be the time when we were moved to the new post in Gradacac.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did you pass by through that checkpoint on more than one occasion?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, multiple times.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Before your Unit went to Gradacac, did you ever see Dusko Tadic there at that checkpoint at Orlovci?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Can you please repeat the question?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Before your Unit and you went to Gradacac, did you ever see Dusko Tadic at that checkpoint at Orlovci?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did see him.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Do you know how many times?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Several times.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Do you know what his job was at that checkpoint, who he was working for?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I knew that he was controlling traffic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Was that for the military or the police?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At that time he was with the police.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Was this before or after he had delivered those goods to your place in Gornji Orlovci?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, that was before because the point had existed there before, and so when he came to my house he was in a police uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Do you know what he was doing then at that time when he came to your house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know, but I know that he was with the police.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: When you say in a police uniform, what do you mean by that? Can you describe it to us?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That police uniform was blue.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Do you know how long he had been working in the police when he came to your house at that time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know how much time he had been with them.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Do you know at that time that he came to your house at Gornji Orlovci to leave his things whether that was a period when he was working at checkpoint Orlovci?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that was the period when he worked at Orlovci.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you. That is all I ask.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Niemann, cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: What is your father's name?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mirko.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Is that his name or his nickname?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: His name is Mirko and they call him "Miro".

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Your mother's name?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Gina.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Do you have any brothers and sisters?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I have a sister.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: What is her name?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Milena Jankovic and her married name, Basic.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Do you have a brother?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: When were you mobilized in 1992? You said in your evidence the partly part, can you tell us when that was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot remember the exact date.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Are you able to remember the month?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: April.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Was this before the takeover of Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: When you were first mobilized where were you stationed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was first stationed in Garevci.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: What were your duties there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was on assignment in an infantry unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Were you patrolling any area or did you control traffic or can you tell us what you were doing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We were on the assignment of protecting the people and preventing conflict.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: At this stage was there any conflict going on in the opstina of Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At that time there was no conflict. I was mobilized.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: What was the name of your Unit?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: 5th Light.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Who was your Commander?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot answer that question.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Why can you not answer that question?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I have not been authorised to do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Who has not authorised you to do so?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think that is something I cannot say.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I ask that the witness be directed to answer the question.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Kay?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: There is no objection, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Sir, you need to answer that question. It relates to the issues in this case and so you should respond to the question, and you are directed to respond to the question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You are thinking of the Commander of the battalion?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: I am thinking of the Commander of your Unit.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Krsic Slobodan.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Can you tell us some of the names of the people that were in your Unit?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Huskic, Dragan.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Can you remember any other people that were in your Unit at any time during 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Dusko Matijas.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Any others?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Slobodan Huskic.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: How many men were in your Unit?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Can you give us a rough idea of how many people were in the Unit?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Up to 100, 110, but I do not know the exact figure.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: What is the rank of Slobodan Krsic, your Commander?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was Captain.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Where was he from?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Do you know what nationality or ethnic group he was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Was he a Muslim, do you think?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Do you think he might have been Croatian?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I said I do not know what nationality he was.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: At the commencement of the attack on Kozarac, the shelling of Kozarac, where was it precisely that your Unit was located?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In Gornji Garevci.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: What part of Gornji Garevci?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The road that passes through the village of Garevci.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Which road is that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is the road separating Garevci from Kozarusa.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: How far was it from the main Banja Luka road, Banja Luka to Prijedor road?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Gornji Garevci?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: No, the place where you were stationed at the time of the attack on Kozarac.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know exactly. I did not measure it.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Can you assist us by giving us some idea?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Five or six kilometres from Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did you stay in that place all the time during the attack on Kozarac or did you move about, did your Unit move about?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It did not move away from that place until our transfer.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: So you stayed in exactly the same spot, did you, on the road?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not on the road. I said the road separating Kozarusa from Gornji Garevci.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: What I am trying to find out is what were you doing during the attack on Kozarac precisely? What were you doing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When the conflict broke out, our task was to protect the Serb people and to pull out the Muslims from the conflict because there were many civilians, women and children.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: These are Muslim women and children?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Pulling them out from the conflict, what does that entail?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It meant saving them from getting killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did it mean removing them from the area, by any chance?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: You tell us what you were doing, especially to the Muslim women and children?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Nothing, we were just saving them.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Saving them -- how were you doing that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Simply, our task was at that time to provide safe passage for people who were in vehicles and otherwise heading for Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: But the area was being attacked by the Serb forces, was it not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. We were defending ourselves then, but we had to save the civilians so that they would not get killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: But were not their Serb forces dropping shells on Kozarac and the surrounding area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is true, but our task was to save the civilians.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: But would not the best way to save the civilians have been to stop the shelling?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is not in my power.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: So you were protecting these people from the shelling, were you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not from the shelling. We were protecting them in that conflict so that they would not get killed, children and the civilians.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: What were you doing with the men, the Muslim men?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Those who were armed were given over to the authorities in Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: What happened to them when they were handed over to the authorities in Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Afterwards they were interrogated and then what happened next, I do not know.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: But these men were not armed, were they?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There were those who were armed.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: I see. Now tell us what you did with the men that were not armed, the Muslim men that were not armed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We also -- we acted towards them in the same way that we treated the women and children.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: That was to direct their traffic towards Prijedor, if I heard you correctly?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Is it not a fact that the women, children and men were put on buses?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is true, they went on buses.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: They were taken to a number of centres, were they not, one in Prijedor at a place called Keraterm, one at Omarska and one in Trnopolje, were they not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am aware only that they were driven to Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Do you know a person called Rade Strika?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Tomislav Stojakovic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Brane Balte?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Goran Grabic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Do you know a place, a coffee shop, called "Kod Zike"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Do you know the area called Velika Kladusa?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: When you say that Dule Tadic brought the goods, refrigerator and so forth, to your house, he came with a Tam truck, did he?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: How long did he stay there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Briefly, to unload the things.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: You said that the shelling of Kozarac only lasted a very short time, was that about a day, was it, or less?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was in one day but it did not last long.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Can you help us a bit in terms of time? Was it half a day, three-quarters of a day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Maybe three-quarters of a day, but with gaps and for a short time.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: When Dule Tadic collected the goods from your house, I think you said you were not there at the time, is that correct, or were you there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I said I was not there because he would take what he needed to his temporary accommodation in Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: He may have taken it there, but you do not know yourself exactly where he took it? He could have taken it somewhere else in Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, he just needed it for the apartment that he got in Prijedor on a temporary basis.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: But you are assuming that is what he did with it, are you not, because you do not know?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: My mother and my father can confirm this.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: But I am asking you what you can confirm.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can just say that he took those things for himself personally, for his own needs.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: You would not argue with me, would you, if I said to you it is possible that some of the goods were taken to some place in Prijedor and others were taken to another place? You do not know, do you? He could have taken them to two places?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is possible, because I did not participate in the transportation of the goods.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: I should have asked you, do you know a place called Velika Kladusa?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Do you know a place called Kozarusa?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Where is that in relation to where you lived?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I lived in Gornji Orlovci. Then comes the village of Garevci and then Kozarusa.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: How far would that be in terms of kilometres, approximately?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: From my place of residence?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: About two, two and a half kilometres.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Are you related to Dusan Jankovic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Do you know Dusan Jankovic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: What was he doing during 1992, do you know?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I just know that he was in the police, but I do not know what his post was.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: How well do you know him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Little.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Have you seen any of these proceedings on television, the proceedings of this Court?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Have you discussed the evidence that you are going to give with any of the witnesses to this case?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: With any members of the family?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I have not.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: You said that Brane Koncar attended your house with Dule Tadic, is that right? Do you remember saying that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: How was he dressed on the day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Brane Koncar?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was in civilian clothes at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: No further questions, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Kay?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: The name "Jankovic", is that a common name, do you know?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is a surname.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Jankovic is a surname.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Are there many people called ----

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is frequent, quite frequent.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you. That is all I ask.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Niemann?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Nothing, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Is there any objection to the witness being permanently excused?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour, there is.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Sir, you are free to leave at this time. However, you may be recalled to give testimony before the Tribunal, so you should make yourself available. Keep in touch with Mr. Kay and, if it is necessary for you to return to give additional testimony, then he will be contacted. Will you do that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Certainly I will. Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Thank you. You are now excused. You are free to leave. Thank you for coming.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Kay, would you call your next witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: The next witness is Ljubomir Tadic, your Honour. ^^ LJUBOMIR TADIC, called.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Sir, would you please take the oath that is being given to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Fine. Thank you. You may be seated. Mr. Kay, you may begin.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Is your name Ljubomir Tadic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I am Ljubomir Tadic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Is your name abbreviated often to "Ljubo"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Whereabouts do you live, Mr. Tadic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Since 1973 I live in Banja Luka.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Whereabouts in Banja Luka, if you could give us the full address?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Josif Pancic Street, No. 6.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: How old are you, Mr. Tadic?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Born on 4th February 1953, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, in Kozarac.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You have no need to lean forward to the microphone. You can stay where you are and it will pick up the sound.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You are the brother of Dusko Tadic, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, older brother.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: The other brothers are Mladen and Stojan, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You are also the son of Ostoja Tadic and Staka Tadic who are the names of your parents?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Are you a married man?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Do you have children?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Three sons.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Their ages are what?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The oldest, Nenad, was born in '79, Vladimir in 1980 and Aleksandar in '92.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Have you done any service in the former JNA?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, but not a complete term of duty.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Can you tell us the period of service?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: What was the reason for not completing the service?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I had some health problems.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: What were they?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Kidneys and some other things, but at the time -- there was an image that you could avoid service if you had connections like father or something, so I was released before my time was up.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: What age did you leave school?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not understand the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: What age did you leave your education, your schooling education?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I left school for apprentice as a welder.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: What age were you when you finished that?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Can you tell us the history of your jobs? First of all, you have told us about being a welder, but was that your first job when you finished your education?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: What was your first job?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: My first job was a professional karate between '73 and '77.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Was this before or after you had been invalided from the JNA?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was doing karate before and after, and I started in '66, '67 as a very young man and I continued to do it to date.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Is it correct that your brother Mladen is also a karate expert?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We all inherited it, so to speak, from him because he was an athlete. In '65, '66, he did it in Belgrade and then he moved to Banja Luka. So that we took it over from him. He left to Germany in '73 and I took over the club and that is how I got into it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Your brother Dusko was also a karate expert, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was not doing it as much until he went to Belgrade and then he joined a karate club at a friend of mine's, Zika Vukojevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: But the other brother, Stojan, is it right that he is not a karate expert?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He is not but in '69 he did train a little in Belgrade while he was studying.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You have told us that you were a karate coach from 1973 to 1977. What was your employment afterwards in 1977?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In '77 my wife was pregnant and so I had to take a more serious approach to things and then got employed at Cajevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Is that a TV factory in Banja Luka?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, but I did not work on television, I worked as a welder. There was -- I had gone through a special training for welding with aluminium. That was something special.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: For how long did you work then as a welder there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I worked for two years, but I remained at the company. I changed my job. They needed a person who could work on supplies, a unit, and they needed somebody who was very active and who could move fast.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: So did you work as a welder then in that factory until 1980?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Then from 1980 did you work as a buyer for the same factory?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I went and did -- went through school and I got qualifications as a salesman, and I passed all the exams for all the driving licences so that I could drive different types of vehicles.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: For what period then did you work as a buyer for that factory in Banja Luka?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: From 1980 until 1990. I am sorry, from -- yes, from 1980 to 1990.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: What happened then in 1990 in relation to your employment?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Rudi Cajavec was declining as a company and then there was an offer, there was surplus, whoever wanted to go into private business would get 24 months worth of salary. Then I talked to my wife and we decided to do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: So during this period that you were working at Rudi Cajavec, is it right that your wife was also employed by the same company?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, in the same company but it was a different department of the same company, Cajavec.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did she also take redundancy as you did with two years salary?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: With that two years salary did you open a general store in Banja Luka?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Just so that we know what that means, what kind of store was that, the size of it and what sorts of products were sold?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There were food products and non-food products, so it was mixed goods.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did you have a shop?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did both you and your wife work there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Does that business still trade today?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: When did it cease trading?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Do you have work today?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: During the period that you have spoken of after you finished your job as a karate coach in 1977, did you continue coaching karate on an amateur basis?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I trained at Karate Club Borac. I continued to do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did you have a part-time job during various periods working as a karate coach in those last 20 years?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I was paid in the evening hours for conducting training. I had a licence so I could do exams all the way up until the black belt, and when some other clubs called me I would go there and I would be paid for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: So the level that you reached within karate was that as a black belt?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Fourth Dan which was the highest at that time in Bosnia and it is also the highest one in the Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: So that we also understand this, your brother Mladen, what level did he reach in karate?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He had a club in Germany in Munich and he had Fifth Dan, that is a step above.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Your other brother Dusko, what level did he reach?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Third Dan.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Of the black belt?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. He was a master.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Were you brought up as a child in Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Was your brother Dusko also brought up there in the family home in Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did there come a time, however, when you left Kozarac to live in Banja Luka?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, in 1973. I already said that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Since then, 1973, have you ever returned to live in Kozarac, and by that I mean live with your own property, your own house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, but I would come often with my family.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: So the place where you have lived ever since has been in Banja Luka, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: How frequently have you visited Kozarac in that 25 years or so or 23 years since you moved to live in Banja Luka?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the first three or four years when I moved to Banja Luka I could not adjust very well to that life. I liked Kozarac and I would come every weekend to Kozarac. I would return.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Your family home in Kozarac has been always in Marsala Tita Street, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, No. 36.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: That house was of a fairly small size originally. Is it right that it has been extended over the years?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, our father was extending it and he was building -- by extending it he was building a bigger one.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I would like you to look at Prosecution Exhibit 300. (Handed). Do you recognise this as being a picture of the family home in Kozarac taken in February of this year?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, but this house, the upper part was built '70 something -- no, I am sorry, before our father died in '89.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Perhaps if ----

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He did all this himself, except for the business down here, the business, except for Dusan's business premises.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Perhaps if that could be put on the monitor to your side so that we can see it. If you would like to turn to your right, Mr. Tadic, and indicate certain parts of the house to us with that steel pointer. Originally the house was the section from the left to the middle, is that right? If you could just indicate the original house that you spoke of.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [The witness indicated]. This part existed only. Afterwards this part was built on, but it was not completed and at first the house did not have an upper floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: When was the upper floor built?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Our father did that. He did it with his own savings. He was a retired officer. He had one of the highest pensions on the territory of the municipality of Prijedor, and he also raised certain loans. As a veteran he could get these loans and he himself built it, not with the resources of us children, but with his own resources.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: The section on the right-hand side, if you could just put the pointer on that, when was that section built?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This was built, completed in 1990 and the shop was opened, but material began to be collected in '88, '89. Dusko was collecting the bricks, the tiles, the wood.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Is there a section of this house which is today a part of the house that is in your name, that is known to belong to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: After our father's death or actually before he died he told us which part belonged to whom and told us not to quarrel over it; when he died that we should state clearly what belonged to whom, as he said it, before the lawyer, and that if you are good children that is what you will do, he said. He said the central part of the building should belong to me. This front part was not like this. There was just a window. It was a dwelling place.
