This part belonged to Stojan and this left incomplete part was given to Mladen, because he was in Germany and we thought that he would find it easier to complete it while those of us who were left in Bosnia had less resources. The upper part which was completed before his death, he said that it should belong to Dusko as he was the youngest and he would stay on to live with our mother in Kozarac, but that a part of this should definitely belong to our mother just in case. Simply that was the kind of man he was. He wanted everyone to know what belonged to him. Each of these parts of buildings has a separate entrance from the other side.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: What year did your father die?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: April 23rd 1989.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: The section we see on the right-hand side, can you tell us when that started to be built?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: After our father's death, but Dusko already had the material ready and he asked our father whether he could build it and our father said to me: "Ljubo, do you agree that we give this part of the land to Dusko because he wants to start a business?" and I said I personally have nothing against, let him build three floors if he likes, if he has the money to do it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: First of all, that section on the right-hand side, if we can talk about the ground floor, can you tell us when work started to build that section?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On the ground floor, this part?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The second half of '79, after the death of our father.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Is that '79 or '89?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am sorry, '89.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: The upper part that we see in red brick, can you tell us when that was started to be built?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When he completed the lower part -- I remember it was customary for this part which had a concrete slab and it was customary for all the people, all the neighbours, to join in and give a hand to complete it. Then we would roast a pig or a lamb on the spit, people would bring drinks and the people participating would not charge anything. They were hosted by the family, and the same would happen when the roof was being put up.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: The bit on the ground floor, was it always intended that that would be a cafe?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Was that to be a business run by your brother Dusko Tadic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: The upper section on the first floor, was that to be living accommodation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: For a time he wanted it for living there, and then once he said he perhaps might open a discotheque there. Anyway, the inside was never completed. To this day it has not been completed of the upper part.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Your brother Stojan who has been mentioned and has that section with the small window we see in the middle, did he live in Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: What has been his work over the years of the 1980s until, let us say, 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He worked in Veletekstil, a large firm, and he was a salesman for that firm. Afterwards he joined a firm from Srenjanin also as a travelling salesman, but he lived in Banja Luka.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: When did he stop that work as a salesman?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When the war started in the former Bosnia-Herzegovina some of his goods were in Bosanski Samac with Mirza, a friend of his who was also a salesman and who had a shop there. So that all those goods were there and when his goods were robbed so was Stojan's.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Does he work as a painter, an artist today presently?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He always engaged in painting, and now his daughter has graduated in Belgrade. She probably got it from her father. She graduated from the school of applied arts, and she is going to go on to the art academy now.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: By the time we get to 1992 is the section on the right-hand side of the photograph, which was where Dusko had his cafe, that was working as a business, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: On the left-hand side, the part that was unfinished that was given to brother Mladen, was that working as a bar in 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Has that bar, which is today a bar, been opened by your brother Mladen after 1992 at a much later date?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He opened it in '90 -- he worked on it in '94. After Dusko's arrest, after some time he too had to leave Germany and he came to Kozarac.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: The middle section which you said was yours and originally had a small window, had that been converted into shop premises before or after the conflict?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I worked on it for several months because I did not have that much money. I worked on it slowly. I was working in Banja Luka. I had a shop there. Then I would come on Saturdays and Sundays, on Friday, Saturday, Sunday, to finish these premises and I opened it maybe 15 days before the outbreak of the conflict in Kozarac.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: What did you open that central section which we see in our photograph as in 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I signed a contract with the Banja Luka brewery and I opened a beer discount shop.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you. Your Honour, that is probably a convenient moment.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: We will adjourn until tomorrow at 10.00 a.m.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: (The court adjourned until the following day).
